messages:
alex: Quick question on API error semantics for /v1/infer — we need a short, consistent rule set for 4xx vs 5xx and what goes in the body. Thinking validation vs runtime vs transient capacity.

maria: Yes please. Are you aiming to change anything for backward compatibility? We should avoid breaking clients.

alex: No breaking changes. Want to document behavior so teams implement retries/handling consistently. Also want example error payloads for SDKs and OpenAPI.

sam: TL;DR proposal:
- 400: bad request / invalid JSON (non-retryable)
- 422: semantic validation (e.g., prompt too long, invalid param value) — non-retryable, include field-level details
- 401/403: auth/permission — non-retryable
- 404: resource not found (model id, route) — non-retryable
- 409: conflicting request (idempotency or model state) — non-retryable, client may retry with changes
- 429: rate limit / quota — retryable, include Retry-After header
- 503: capacity / temporary service degraded — retryable, include Retry-After if possible
- 500/502/504: server errors — treat as retryable for idempotent ops (but client should backoff)

maria: This looks sane. One question: 422 vs 400 boundary — we should give concrete rules.

jin: Our current behavior is inconsistent: sometimes we return 400 for missing fields, sometimes 422. We should standardize.

alex: Proposed rule: 400 = syntactic problems (malformed JSON, wrong content-type, cannot parse body). 422 = semantic validation (schema OK but values invalid or business rule failed). Example: 
- Bad JSON -> 400
- "model" field present but unknown value -> 422 (with error.code = "invalid_model")

sam: Agree. Also suggest using problem+json-ish envelope we already use: error: { code, message, details? } and numeric http status separately. Keep human message in message and machine code in code.

maria: Can we add an example payload for SDKs?

alex: Sure, example for a validation error:
```json
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": {
    "code": "prompt_too_long",
    "message": "Prompt exceeds max tokens (32768)",
    "details": [
      { "path": "input.prompt", "reason": "length", "max": 32768 }
    ]
  }
}
```

alex: Example for rate limit:
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": {
    "code": "rate_limit",
    "message": "Request quota exceeded",
    "retry_after_seconds": 30
  }
}
```

jin: For 503 we should indicate if the request is safe to retry immediately or if it will likely fail for a while. Maybe a short hint in message or retry_after_seconds.

sam: We should also document idempotency guidance: POSTish endpoints that create jobs should accept Idempotency-Key and return 409 or the existing resource if key repeated. That way SDKs can retry safely.

maria: Back-compat note: if we add new error.code strings, clients should not break — encourage SDKs to inspect category (4xx vs 5xx) or code prefix rather than exact match. Add tests to assert old codes still returned for existing checks.

alex: Action items: @maria to update /v1/infer OpenAPI and error sections, @sam to add unit tests for consistent status mapping, @jin to sweep runtime code paths that return 400 vs 422. I'll open a small RFC PR.

maria: Ack. I'll also add a short section in the console docs describing which errors are retryable and showing example JS fetch handling.

sam: Quick fetch example to show retry logic (to include in docs):
```js
async function callInfer(payload){
  const res = await fetch('/v1/infer', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload) });
  if (res.status === 429 || res.status === 503 || res.status >= 500) {
    // exponential backoff + jitter
  } else if (res.status === 422) {
    const body = await res.json();
    // show validation errors to user, don't retry
  }
}
```

jin: Also add an integration test that asserts a malformed JSON returns 400 with a short machine code like "bad_request" so SDKs can map it quickly.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: docs-rfc -> staging at 2026-03-17T18:00Z :rocket:

alex: Thanks all. I'll draft the RFC and link tests. Ping me if you see any edge cases (e.g., multipart uploads, streaming chunk errors).

maria: One more edge: streaming responses that fail mid-stream — we should return a final status code in the termination message or reason header. Will add that note.

sam: Cool. I'll add a lint rule to forbid returning plain text 500 bodies; must be JSON envelope.

alex: Perfect. Closing this thread — expect PR in an hour. :thumbsup:
